# A conditional with a comment after the question mark, at the end of the
# true branch or after the colon is not rewritten with -s, since the
# rewritten form has no position for the comment. It is written as it is
# without -s.
celfmt -i question.cel
! stderr .
cp stdout want_question.txt
celfmt -s -i question.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_question.txt
stdout '// why'

celfmt -i access.cel
! stderr .
cp stdout want_access.txt
celfmt -s -i access.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_access.txt
stdout '// why'

celfmt -i colon.cel
! stderr .
cp stdout want_colon.txt
celfmt -s -i colon.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_colon.txt
stdout '// why'

# The same holds for the negated form, where the false branch is the access.
celfmt -i negated.cel
! stderr .
cp stdout want_negated.txt
celfmt -s -i negated.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_negated.txt
stdout '// why'

celfmt -i negated_question.cel
! stderr .
cp stdout want_negated_question.txt
celfmt -s -i negated_question.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_negated_question.txt
stdout '// why'

# The same inside a macro call.
celfmt -i macro.cel
! stderr .
cp stdout want_macro.txt
celfmt -s -i macro.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_macro.txt
stdout '// why'

# Without a comment it is rewritten.
celfmt -s -i plain.cel
! stderr .
stdout 'state.x.\?f.orValue'

-- question.cel --
has(state.x.f) ? // why
	state.x.f
:
	"default"
-- access.cel --
has(state.x.f) ?
	state.x.f // why
:
	"default"
-- colon.cel --
has(state.x.f) ?
	state.x.f
: // why
	"default"
-- plain.cel --
has(state.x.f) ?
	state.x.f
:
	"default"
-- negated.cel --
!has(state.x.f) ?
	"default"
: // why
	state.x.f
-- negated_question.cel --
!has(state.x.f) ? // why
	"default"
:
	state.x.f
-- macro.cel --
state.items.map(e,
	has(e.f) ? // why
		e.f
	:
		"default"
)
